svg.text: DISH · how it goes together
Exploded side view (from the right), front at the left · 1 mm = 6.6 px
The base is SLAB's core with a round well cut in the middle. The dish is its own small instrument: a round
PCB with its own MCU that talks to the base over 4 wires through the hollow pivots. Numbers = build steps (17).
Checked against eng v2 §2, §4.1, §4.2 · common-how-it-works §1 (joint rule), §5 · dish/how-it-works
Dish: caps + round face PCB (13 pots/rotaries + hero, 4067, light ring)
dish MCU board on its back; back skin is a second canvas
Brass axle tube across the fork tips + 2 laser-stacked fork arms
pivot at the well's rear; 4-core silicone cable runs through both tubes
Wings: low caps on board A, panels sunk 8 mm
analog tone controls in the audio path (eng §2 knob-only)
Board B under the wings + low-profile B extension under the well
≤ 8 mm parts only under the well floor (E7)
Ø40 driver (≤ 12 mm deep) + chamber at the well centre
grille in the well floor
Base: ≈ 12 laser layers (walnut ply), the well cut through the top 8
fork channels beside the well
Keys: bought maple button plugs on drilled blank caps
on Gateron low-profile Hall switches; felt collar per hole
Board D + 2 LiPo pouch cells under the keys
Base plate, screws, felt feet
← player (front)
